## Google Scholar Search Results: binary coverage-guided fuzz testing Bluetooth controller emulation Chen 2026

### 1. Uncovering Bluetooth vulnerabilities with binary coverage-guided fuzz testing and controller emulation
- **URL**: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167404826001057
- **Publication**: ZM Chen, TC Lin, GY Yang, YS Lin, F Wang, KH YehComputers & Security, 2026•Elsevier
- **Cited by**: 0
- **Abstract**: Bluetooth Basic Rate and Enhanced Data Rate (BR/EDR) is a typical wireless transmission technology in embedded devices and personal computers. Recently, some Bluetooth fuzzing studies have been conducted to identify vulnerabilities in devices and chips; however, they primarily focus on low-level aspects of the Bluetooth stack, and many rely on physical devices to deliver packets. This paper proposes FuBuKi, a binary coverage-guided Bluetooth fuzzer, to detect Bluetooth vulnerabilities on emulated Bluetooth controllers. FuBuKi can generate and mutate the input with binary code coverage by constructing the corresponding input transformer. Furthermore, FuBuKi can emulate the real-world target binaries and successfully discover crashes with a dedicated input transformer. We applied FuBuKi on three different types of Bluetooth stacks with five different profiles to verify the effectiveness. The results of the experiment confirm that FuBuKi is also able to fuzz profiles that require pairing and bonding mechanisms, compared to other state-of-the-art work.
